title: Hong Kong 3D
about:
Hong Kong: both shores of Victoria Harbour. Hong Kong Island's north shore from Kennedy Town to Chai Wan with the Mid-Levels and the Peak; Kowloon from Tsim Sha Tsui and West Kowloon up to the Lion Rock ridge, with Kai Tak, Kwun Tong and Lei Yue Mun; east of the ridge Tseung Kwan O, Clear Water Bay and Sai Kung town. Around them the ground to about 3 km, the new towns beyond it as plain blocks, and the hills to about 20 km (Tai Mo Shan, Lantau).

Real, from open data, each thing where it is: the buildings' footprints and heights (about 54,800; the Lands Department's Building layer, each tower and podium block to its surveyed roof, measured from the lowest ground round it; OpenStreetMap only where the survey has nothing, all under 20 m); the ground from the CEDD's 2020 airborne LiDAR survey (bare earth, averaged to 2 m), the Lands Department's 5 m terrain model beyond it and Copernicus GLO-30 for the hills across the border; roads and flyovers, footbridges, rail and the tramway, piers, water, parks, cut slopes, bare rock and land use from OpenStreetMap; the hills' woods, scrub and grass where OpenStreetMap maps none, and the far land's colours, from ESA WorldCover 2021; the landmarks' heights from published figures (Wikipedia, the CTBUH) checked against the survey; the sun of 5 November, clock time HKT.

Inferred from real attributes: the buildings' kinds and facade styles (public housing estates, private towers, tong lau, composite buildings, flatted factories, offices, malls and podiums, village houses, colonial civic buildings) from the survey's names, block types and heights and OpenStreetMap's tags; 77 blocks whose surveyed roof is too low for their storeys raised to their storeys; the ground under 126 blocks standing over 2020 excavations (the street round them); temporary structures without a height (one storey).

Modelled after photos, not measured: the landmark figures (the Bank of China Tower's prisms, frame and masts, Central Plaza's pyramid and mast, The Center's top, the IFC and ICC crowns and skins, the Government Headquarters' open door, the Convention Centre's wing roof, the Cultural Centre's roofs and the Space Museum's dome, the Clock Tower, M+'s screen, the Peak Tower, Kai Tak Stadium, the ferry piers, the towers' crowns, and the Stonecutters, Tsing Ma, Kap Shui Mun and Cross Bay Link bridges): shapes from photos and published dimensions, several of them estimated; crowns without a photo are generic.

Invented to look plausible: the facades (window grids, wall colours, balconies, bay windows, air-conditioner boxes, shop fronts and shutters, curtains); the projecting street signs (where, how many, their colours; their Chinese characters are common shop words in random order, no real shop's name); the rooftop plant, tanks and huts and the lit boards and crown lights on the towers (no real logos); the trees along the streets and in the parks (the region's species, no tree inventory); the cars, buses, minibuses, taxis and trams, where they drive and where they park; the road markings' layout; the shore types; which windows are lit at night, the floodlights, the street lighting (procedural: no lamp inventory) and the glow. Beyond the districts the new towns (Sha Tin, Kwai Chung, Tsing Yi, Tsuen Wan) are OpenStreetMap's buildings of 30 m and more as plain blocks, the rest a painted roofscape.

Not shown: ships, ferries and boats; people; the harbour's light show; the Peak Tram; Ting Kau Bridge; the container terminals' stacks and cranes. The terrain is the 2020 survey's (a few later platforms stand on the older ground); LandsD's roofs leave out some crowns, drawn as figures only where photographed.

Contains modified Copernicus DEM GLO-30 data © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved. Landmark heights from Wikipedia and the CTBUH (facts, no text copied); reference photos from Wikimedia Commons were only looked at, not redistributed. The derived data this page loads (the tiles, blocks, markings, trees, cars, rooftops and shores beside this page, made by this repository's pipeline) is a derivative database of OpenStreetMap, offered under the Open Database License 1.0; the rendered images are Produced Works, attributed as above. Rendered with three.js and its meshoptimizer decoder (both MIT licence).

switchTitles.rooftops: Parapets, lift motor rooms, water tanks, aerials, huts and plant on the roofs, the lit boards on the towers and the projecting street signs on the shop streets (all invented)
switchTitles.masses: The new towns beyond the districts (Sha Tin, Kwai Chung, Tsing Yi, Tsuen Wan): OpenStreetMap's buildings of 30 m and more as plain blocks, heights from their storeys; the low town between them stays painted
